::: {#def-marginal-likelihood}
#### Marginal likelihood (evidence)

Given a prior $\p(\param)$
and a model $\p(\vy \mid \param)$ for the data given $\param$,
the **marginal likelihood** (also called the **evidence**)
of observed data $\vy$ is

$$
\p(\vy) \eqdef \int_{\Paramspace} \p(\vy \mid \param)\, \p(\param)\, d\param,
$$

where the integral is over the [parameter space](#def-parameter-space) $\Paramspace$,
and is replaced by a sum over the possible values of $\param$
when $\param$ is discrete.

Source: @wikipedia_marginal_likelihood.
:::
